conn.title: Connections & API
conn.intro: Every outside service the factory uses: what it is for, whether it works, and whether it is real or a test. Secrets are sealed and never shown.

connect.title: Connect a service
connect.subtitle: What each service does for the factory, and which ones are connected.
connect.heldTitle: Connecting a service from this page comes later
connect.heldBody: Today Nexus support connects a service for you: it stores the keys sealed on the server, in test mode first. Once connected, the service appears in the list, where you can follow it, pause it and resume it.
connect.held: Not available yet: ask Nexus support to connect this service.

SES.name: Sending e-mail (Amazon SES)
SES.for: Quotes, purchase orders and notifications leave from your own domain; replies come back to their record.
SES.how: One for every company: the mail domain below says which addresses it sends from.

R2.name: File storage (Cloudflare R2)
R2.for: Keeps the files of every record: PDFs, photos, certificates, imported sheets.

SDI.name: E-invoices (SDI)
SDI.for: Sends invoices to the Italian tax system (Sistema di Interscambio) and brings back its receipts.
SDI.how: One per company: each company issues its own invoices.

SENDCLOUD.name: Carrier labels (Sendcloud)
SENDCLOUD.for: Buys shipping labels and follows parcels until they are delivered.
SENDCLOUD.how: One per company: labels are paid by the company that ships.

VIES.name: VAT check (VIES)
VIES.for: Checks EU customers’ and suppliers’ VAT numbers with the European Commission.

delivery.title: Delivery log and blocked addresses
delivery.intro: Every mail the factory sent and where it is now: waiting, sent, delivered, bounced or complained about, or failed. A mail that bounced for good or drew a complaint blocks its address: no more mail goes there until you unblock it.
delivery.masked: Some addresses are masked: only people who manage that company's mail see them in full.
delivery.maskedHint: Masked: only people who manage this company's mail see the address in full.
delivery.emptyBody: Mail appears here as soon as a quote, an order, an invoice or a sign-in mail leaves the factory.

tileHint.WAITING: Queued or being sent now (last 30 days).
tileHint.SENT: The mail service took them; no word back yet (last 30 days).
tileHint.DELIVERED: The recipient's mail server accepted them (last 30 days).
tileHint.PROBLEM: They bounced for good or the recipient marked them as spam: the address is blocked (last 30 days).
tileHint.FAILED: They never left: refused, or out of tries (last 30 days).

problem.bounced: Bounced: the mailbox does not exist or refuses mail.
problem.complained: The recipient marked it as spam.

blocked.title: Blocked addresses
blocked.intro: No mail goes to these addresses. Each one bounced for good, complained, or was stopped by a person. Unblock one only when the problem is fixed.
blocked.emptyBody: When a mail bounces for good or a recipient complains, the address shows up here.
blocked.noneToUnblock: None of the selected addresses is blocked: nothing to unblock.
blocked.heldRight: Unblocking needs the right to unblock addresses over every company (one list serves all of them).

left.unblocked_one: 1 selected address is unblocked already: left out.
left.unblocked_other: {count} selected addresses are unblocked already: left out.

blocked.confirmBody: From now on mail may go to these addresses again. If one bounces for good again, it is blocked again by itself.
blocked.confirmAgain: The row stays in the list of unblocked addresses, with when and why.
blocked.complaintTitle: A recipient marked our mail as spam
blocked.complaintBody: Write to them again only if they asked for it: unblocking does not change what they told their mail service.
blocked.reasonHint: Required. Kept with the change (for example: the customer fixed their mailbox).
blocked.reasonShort: Say why in at least 3 letters.
blocked.unblockedDone_one: 1 address unblocked: mail may go to it again.
blocked.unblockedDone_other: {count} addresses unblocked: mail may go to them again.
blocked.unblockedFailed_other: No address unblocked ({count} refused). Not unblocked:

mail.title: Your mail domain
mail.intro: Send and receive mail from your own domain. Add these records where your domain is registered; Nexus checks them with the mail service.

add.title: Add a sending domain
add.subtitle: The mail service gives three records to add at your registrar; mail leaves from the domain once they are found.
add.accountHint: The connection that sends this domain’s mail.
add.domainHint: A domain you own, or a part of it such as mail.example.com.
add.stepUp: Adding a domain changes who your mail appears to come from: it asks for a fresh code from your authenticator app.

held.noSes: No mail service is connected yet: connect e-mail first.
held.noCompany: Seeing the companies is needed to choose whose domain it is.

empty.title: No sending domain yet
empty.body: Connect e-mail first: everything that leaves the factory needs it.

rule.title: How replies find their record
rule.reply: Each order, request for quote and purchase order gets a hidden reply address on your reply domain; a reply lands in that record’s thread.
rule.checks: A mail joins a thread only when it passes SPF, DKIM and DMARC and the sender is known; otherwise it waits in Mail to sort.
rule.capture: A capture address (forward or copy any mail to it) comes later.

kindHint.CONVERSATION: Quotes, orders and replies, sent by a person.

banner.failed: The mail service could not verify this domain: check each record below, fix it at your registrar, then check again.
banner.disabled: This sending address is switched off: no mail leaves from it.
